newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mixed Australian stocks end barely changed.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Australian stocks end barely changed.

text.p: A mixed Australian share market closed barely changed on Thursday, led back towards square by a futures market that rebounded off its lows in the afternoon.
The All Ordinaries index lost 0.6 points to 2,435.2.

Brokers said the finish was better than expected with the market holding the line in the face of a weak Wall Street, a bond market battered by stronger than expected wages data and a disappointing News Corp first half net profit of A$731 million.
"It's not done too badly considering the Dow was down and the bond market took a hit," said a Melbourne broker.
Others agreed, saying the rebound in the March SPI contract in the afternoon had lifted the underlying market off its lows.
"The end result was fairly pleasing," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.
"Most stocks came off their lows and the market came back step by step with the SPI (futures)."
While most of the leaders ended weaker, enough of the major stocks made very modest gains to compensate.
In the miners, gold/nickel miner WMC held in the black, its shares ending a cent higher at A$8.06 (US$6.14).

Zinc producer Pasminco also gained ground, its shares closing five cents higher at A$2.32 with brokers saying the outlook was positive for some of the base metals miners, especially those leveraged to zinc, nickel or aluminium.

In the banks, Commonwealth Bank continued to be keenly sought by value and dividend hungry investors. Its shares, up 24 cents to a record high A$13.35, single handedly dragged the banking sector to a firmer close.
"CommBank shares are still playing catch-up to the rest of the banks," the dealer said.

Major retailers Woolworths and Coles Myer stayed in positive territory, with Woolworths ending two cents higher at A$3.35 and Coles one cent higher at A$5.06. Brokers said concerns about the sector may have been overdone.

At the smaller end, Gawler Craton gold hopeful Helix Resources was well-supported and reached a record high of A$4.70 on drilling speculation and possible corporate activity. Trade was dominated by the sale of Ashton Mining's 12.9 percent stake.
Preston Resources also jumped ahead, up 28 percent to A$1.06, after it acquired an option over the Marlborough nickel-cobalt deposit in central Queensland.
